I've attached our usage summary and an outline of the expansion ask. Can we schedule a 30-minute call this week to align? Jacob (cc'd) will handle procurement.

Thanks for the summary, Mateo. Finance is comfortable with a $25k one-time credit for this expansion; we should structure it as a non-recoupable invoice credit spread over the first two billing cycles to keep ARR intact.

On the anchor and true-up: recommend the following mechanism to protect us while keeping the customer comfortable:
- 12-month price anchor capped at +3% vs current rate, conditioned on a 30% minimum average monthly commit over the 12-month term.
- True-up clause: if actual monthly consumption exceeds committed by >40% for two consecutive months, we reserve the right to move excess to pay-as-you-go rates for the following month(s) until usage normalizes.
- Temporary burst buffer: +20% burst for first 90 days, then re-evaluate.

If Ben is good, I'll draft the short commercial term sheet and loop Legal for a limited amendment (no full contract rewrite).

Hi Elena and Jacob,

Great to meet on Thursday — thanks for the time. Per our discussion and internal approvals, here's the agreed commercial summary to move to a short amendment: 

1) Pricing anchor: 12 months, capped at +3% vs your current effective rate, conditioned on a 30% uplift in committed monthly units (minimum average over the 12-month term).
2) Onboarding credit: $25,000 one-time credit applied as $12,500 credit on invoice 1 and $12,500 on invoice 2.
3) Burst capacity: Temporary +20% burst buffer for the first 90 days post-effective date.
4) True-up: If consumption exceeds committed volume by >40% for two consecutive months, excess usage will be billed at pay-as-you-go rates until usage returns within threshold.

Next steps: Marissa will circulate a 1-page amendment and I'll follow with a DocuSign link. Once signed we can schedule the migration work with our onboarding team.

Links: HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/deals/4832) — DocuSign to follow.
